summary: Trinity County cabin lookout on a rugged point: work began in 1933, an observer in 1937, then a slide and abandonment that October; FFLA lists it as gone.

facts.design: Cabin anchored to bedrock with iron rods set in sulphur, with a catwalk around it (1937 newspaper item)
facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as Gone; no source read gives a removal date

events.note: Foundations were being prepared in October 1933; by November a new lookout was described as under way (newspaper items transcribed by Forest Lookouts)
Joe Strunce served as observer, per a June 1937 newspaper item
Station was in great demand for Forest Service radio relay work, per a June 1937 newspaper item
Per an October 9, 1937 item, during a storm the previous week part of the rocky summit slid beneath the station; the station was abandoned for the winter

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. A 1933 item gives the point as about 6,500 feet; a 1937 item places the station on a 7,000-foot divide. The story reports both figures and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: All history comes from newspaper items that Forest Lookouts transcribes; the original papers were not opened. The brief record (Trinity County, ground type, status gone, coordinates) matches the FFLA county list, so no corrections. No source read gives a removal date, a cause of removal, or what remains at the site. The firetower.org and nhlr.org URLs for Cabin Peak returned 404. The access key is omitted because no source gives an access level, and the story says so. Construction is dated from October to November 1933 with no completion date.
